o:
We must split `nums` into contiguous blocks whose XORs alternate `target1, target2, target1, ...`. Using prefix XORs `P[i]`, a block `(j, i]` has XOR `P[i]^P[j]`. So a valid partition corresponds to a walk over prefix values where each step's XOR alternates between the two targets. With `n` up to 1e5 we need better than examining all O(n^2) block boundaries naively, which suggests hashing prefix XOR values while running a DP.

Example 1: prefixes are 0,2,1,0,4. The only valid cut structure is one block ending where prefix jumps by `target1=1` (at index 1) followed by a block jumping by `target2=5` (index 3), giving 1 partition. Example 2: `[1|0|0]` and `[1|0,0]` and `[1,0,0]` all work because prefix values repeat, letting multiple boundaries produce the required XORs.
k: Block XORs reduce to differences of prefix XORs, so transitions only depend on prefix values, not positions.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute-force DP over cut positions
a.i: Let `dp0[i]` = number of ways to partition the prefix of length `i` into an even number of blocks (so the next block must equal `target1`) and `dp1[i]` similarly for odd. For every pair `(j, i)` check whether `P[i]^P[j]` equals the required target and accumulate. This is O(n^2) but makes the recurrence obvious.
s: For each i, loop over all j<i: if P[i]^P[j]==target1 add dp0[j] to dp1[i]; if it equals target2 add dp1[j] to dp0[i].
a.t: O(n^2) — all pairs of prefix indices are examined
a.sp: O(n) — prefix array and two DP arrays

a.n: Approach 2: Hash map over prefix XOR values (optimal)
a.i: The transition for position `i` only needs the total DP weight stored at prefix value `P[i]^target1` (for odd-count states feeding an even extension) and `P[i]^target2`. Keep two hash maps from prefix XOR value to aggregated DP sums, updated in one pass. Since `target1 != target2`, the two lookups never interfere.
s: Maintain maps even/odd: prefixXor -> summed DP weights; even = {0: 1}.
Walk the array maintaining running prefix p.
At each step: newOdd[p] += even[p^target1]; newEven[p] += odd[p^target2].
Return even[p] at the final prefix.
a.t: O(n) expected — one hash-map pass over prefixes
a.sp: O(n) — hash maps hold at most n+1 prefix values

w: Use the hash-map DP in an interview; the brute force is only for validating logic. Pitfalls: forgetting the empty-prefix base case (a single block equal to target1 must be counted), and confusing which parity consumes target1 vs target2. Follow-ups: what if target1 == target2 (then every block equals the same value and the parity distinction collapses), or if blocks had length limits.
